title: C section pooch gets a second chance?
text: I had a classical c section for for my first, and I couldn’t wear a belly band as I found it too painful. I ended up getting the dreaded  shelf. now that I’m pregnant with my second  since the belly will stretch again so I wonder if I’ll get a second chance to fix my pooch. I’m wondering if I put a belly band this time, will it somewhat correct the pooch? I don’t expect it to go away, any improvement will help my confidence!!

Item didn’t work well for me. B belly shaped and bottom constantly rode up defeating the purpose. Top band tended to dig in and be uncomfortable no matter how it was adjusted. I didn’t have the original packaging to returning wasn’t super easy and I had to talk with support. Although they did finally allow it after I kept pushing the issue.
Didn’t work. Velcro wouldn’t stay latched.
I want to love it. But it comes loose completely. It doesn’t stay in place. I did buy the correct size. And the back is very rough and itchy.

title: Reminder to wear your belly band even if you don’t think you need it yet!
text:
I’m 20 weeks and haven‘t stopped working out since I found out I was pregnant. I do modified kickboxing 3 times a week and runs every now and again. I got my belly band two months ago but kept looking at it like, “I don’t need you yet” since I really wasn’t showing.

  
Well, the strain on my pelvis and hips has been creeping up and I didn’t really notice it. My Monday workout TOOK me out and I had so much pelvic pain I couldn’t sleep. Strapped my belly band on for class this evening and holy cow, what a difference. I’m still wearing it right now because the weight off my pelvis and lower back is incredible. 

  
Wish I had started wearing it a month ago!

title: Turning in my sleep is excruciating
text:
FTM, 38+5 weeks pregnant, I have all the pregnancy pillows that everyone recommends shoved under me and around me during sleep, and it doesn't make a difference to the pain.

When I turn from one side to the other, my huge belly pulls on my ligaments so hard that the pain is unbearable. It takes ages to get up the strength to turn over, sometimes I have to wake my husband up and get him to help hoist me up.

I used to be able to tuck my knees up as high as they'd go to my chest and then roll, but I can't make this movement anymore. 

Last night I broke down and for the last couple hours wore my belly band while sleeping, which helped support my muscles when turning, but the instruction manual says not to do that and I know by relying on it too much I am making my own muscles weaker.

I just don't know what to do anymore and getting through the last couple weeks of this pregnancy seems impossible. Looking for any advice from people who might've experienced this.
So supportive and helps round out belly to make me feel more confident in my body style 😌
I loved wearing clothes that showed off my belly. I thought crop tops were so cute. Even a cute Lil sweater over a bodysuit/romper was sooo cute. I could wear my belly band and no one could tell.

I never wore a belly band with my first pregnancy. But I have so much pelvic pressure, & hip pain at 27 weeks I thought I would try! Loooove the stretch, the comfort & support and it definitely helps relieve pressure! I got a large & love it!
Helps with backpain and makes the bump look more prominent
Love this!  Supports and if comfortable for daily wear!
Love this 🫶🏼

title: 25+2 and running isn’t fun
text: Hey everyone, I love this group and trying not to totally compare to some of you baddies that are making me feel super inadequate 😂I’ve been struggling the past 5 weeks or so with pelvic floor discomfort when I run. I started pelvic floor PT and use a belly band but it’s just not comfortable anymore, and run-walk for 3 miles is pretty much my max. Pre pregnancy I was in a marathon training cycle and even if I wasn’t training I was generally getting about 20 miles per week. I guess I just see a lot of you still talking about running until 30 weeks plus and so is this really abnormal? My plan is to transition to elliptical and swimming over the summer, but I want to keep running “as long as possible” if it’s not painful. Thanks for your takes!!

I got a belly band and that helps give my growing belly support. I have a ton of round ligament pain and lower back pain. I take warm salt baths often and soak for an hour or more. My husband also rubs my lower back probably every night. I got a heated blanket that I lay on on the couch so it's against my lower back and that feels good. Sometimes an ice pack on my lower back helps. Tylenol when I can't take it and also just crying for a min. 

I also have access to a swimming pool that I walk around in regularly for exercise and that really helps take the extra weight off my joints and feels good.
This has been awesome for working out with my growing bump!

Bought for my daughter and she said it’s a huge help in holding up her little bundle and easing her pelvic pain. The material is soft, so it’s not scratchy against the skin. And the Velcro fasteners are strong and easily adjustable.

title: Someone help me find a good belly band please!
text:
Hi 🫶 I'm in my second pregnancy 24 weeks along. I have had some severe muscle pain around the belly button associated with moderate activity/lifting and a bad case of diastasis recti. My OB gave me a 20 lb lift restriction (unfortunately I am a nurse and have a 33 lb toddler so this is hard) and recommended a good belly band and KT tape.

Are there any that are particularly good for diastasis recti during pregnancy? I honestly hated my belly band my first pregnancy because it felt so restrictive and uncomfortable. Thanks!!
